relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a person with a clinical diagnosis of Tangier disease ("A 24-year-old male was diagnosed with Tangier disease"); no ABCA1 variant or genetic testing is mentioned, so the person is in scope by diagnosis only and has no variant rows.
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short script, values typed from reading. No ABCA1 gene or variant is named anywhere in the paper, so the variants table is empty. Age '24-year-old' is attached to the sentence 'was diagnosed with Tangier disease' and recorded as age at diagnosis; it may equally be his age at presentation. Year of publication is not printed in the text, so year is null. n_patients_reported is null because the authors state no patient with an ABCA1 variant; cohort size 1 from the title. 'apoprotein A < 5 mg/dl' does not say apolipoprotein A-I, so checklist 'low apolipoprotein A-I' is left not reported (feature row kept). Triglycerides 100 mg/dl are printed with a garbled reference range '(normal: 170350)' and are not called normal or abnormal, so hypertriglyceridemia is not reported and no feature row was made. 'The physical exploration was normal.' is a whole-examination statement: recorded as written (abnormal physical exploration, excluded) and used to exclude nothing more specific (spleen, liver, lymph nodes, tonsils stay not reported). 'No orange tonsils' excludes orange tonsils only; the composite checklist item 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' stays not reported. Lipid deposits were found in gastric (antral) mucosa, which is not intestinal mucosa, and the duodenum was normal; a duodenal absence does not exclude the broader 'intestinal mucosal lipid deposits', so that item is not reported. Normal laboratory list (transaminases, coagulation, orosomucoid, CRP, antigliadin and antitransglutaminase antibodies, fat-soluble vitamins, fecal chemotrypsin) recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27. 'He had no family history' is not a phenotype and was not recorded. Vital status not stated. Discussion mentions a previously described absence of orange tonsils and a rectal mucosa report (ref 5) without an individual-level description of a person; no row created. No contradictions found.
